question.text: Two coils have mutual inductance <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>002</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi></math>. The current changes in the first coil according to the relation <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>i</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mi>s</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>ω</mi><mi>t</mi></math>, where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>i</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>ω</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>50</mn><mi>π</mi></math> <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>rad</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The maximum value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>emf</mi></math> in the second coil is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mi>α</mi></mfrac><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>α</mi></math> is

solution.text:
The amount of flux induced in the second coil due to the first one is given by

ϕ2=Mi=Mi0sinωt   ...1

where, M is the mutual inductance of the coils.

The formula to calculate the emf induced can be written as

ε=-dϕ2dt   ...2

From equation (2), it follows that,

εmax=Mi0ω=0.002×5×50π V=π2 V

Hence, α=2.
